if: financial statements are being prepared and presented
one of the fundamental accounting assumptions — Going Concern, Consistency or Accrual — is NOT followed
then: the FACT that it is not followed MUST be disclosed
note: The obligation is inverted from the usual direction: following the assumptions requires no disclosure at all, so silence asserts that all three hold. AS 1 does not require the amount of the departure to be disclosed under this paragraph — only the fact.

evidence.quote: If the fundamental accounting assumptions, viz. Going Concern, Consistency and Accrual are followed in financial statements, specific disclosure is not required. If a fundamental accounting assumption is not followed, the fact should be disclosed.
They are usually not specifically stated because their acceptance and use are assumed. Disclosure is necessary if they are not followed.
